name: BESSELI

args.name: x
args.about: the value to work out the function at

args.name: n
args.about: the order, a whole number 0 or more

about: Gives the modified Bessel function In(x), used for waves in round things.

example.why: The modified Bessel function of order 1 at 1.5 is about 0.9817.

name: BESSELJ

args.name: x
args.about: the value to work out the function at

args.name: n
args.about: the order, a whole number 0 or more

about: Gives the Bessel function Jn(x), used for vibrating drums and waves.

example.why: The Bessel function of order 2 at 1.9 is about 0.3299.

name: BESSELK

args.name: x
args.about: the value to work out the function at

args.name: n
args.about: the order, a whole number 0 or more

about: Gives the modified Bessel function Kn(x), which fades away as x grows.

example.why: The modified Bessel function of the second kind, order 1, at 1.5 is about 0.2774.

name: BESSELY

args.name: x
args.about: the value to work out the function at

args.name: n
args.about: the order, a whole number 0 or more

about: Gives the Bessel function Yn(x), the second kind of Bessel function.

example.why: The Bessel function of the second kind, order 1, at 2.5 is about 0.1459.

name: ERF

args.name: lower_limit
args.about: where to start (or the end, from 0, if upper_limit is left out)

args.name: upper_limit
args.about: where to stop

about: Gives the error function, used for the spread of measurement errors.

example.why: The error function from 0 to 1 is about 0.8427.

notes: With two limits it gives the error function between them.

name: ERFC

args.name: x
args.about: the value to work out the function at

about: Gives 1 minus the error function: the part beyond x.

name: ERFC.PRECISE

args.name: x
args.about: the value to work out the function at

about: Gives 1 minus the error function: the part beyond x.

name: ERF.PRECISE

args.name: x
args.about: the value to work out the function at

about: Gives the error function from 0 to x.

example.why: The error function from 0 to 1 is about 0.8427.

notes: The same as ERF with one limit.

name: BIN2DEC

args.name: number
args.about: a binary number of up to 10 digits

about: Turns a binary number into a decimal number.
notes: Ten digits starting with 1 count as negative.

name: BIN2HEX

args.name: number
args.about: a binary number of up to 10 digits

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a binary number into hexadecimal.

example.why: 11111011 is 251, which is FB in hexadecimal.

name: BIN2OCT

args.name: number
args.about: a binary number of up to 10 digits

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a binary number into octal.

example.why: 1001 is 9, which is 11 in octal, padded to 3 digits.

name: DEC2BIN

args.name: number
args.about: a whole number from -512 to 511

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a decimal number into binary.

name: DEC2HEX

args.name: number
args.about: a whole number

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a decimal number into hexadecimal.

name: DEC2OCT

args.name: number
args.about: a whole number

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a decimal number into octal.

name: HEX2BIN

args.name: number
args.about: a hexadecimal number of up to 10 digits

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a hexadecimal number into binary.

example.why: F is 15, which is 1111 in binary, padded to 8 digits.

name: HEX2DEC

args.name: number
args.about: a hexadecimal number of up to 10 digits

about: Turns a hexadecimal number into a decimal number.

name: HEX2OCT

args.name: number
args.about: a hexadecimal number of up to 10 digits

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a hexadecimal number into octal.

name: OCT2BIN

args.name: number
args.about: an octal number of up to 10 digits

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a octal number into binary.

example.why: 7 is 111 in binary, padded to 4 digits.

name: OCT2DEC

args.name: number
args.about: an octal number of up to 10 digits

about: Turns a octal number into a decimal number.

name: OCT2HEX

args.name: number
args.about: an octal number of up to 10 digits

args.name: places
args.about: how many digits to show, padded with zeros

about: Turns a octal number into hexadecimal.

example.why: 100 in octal is 64, which is 40 in hexadecimal, padded to 4 digits.

name: BITAND

args.name: number1
args.about: a whole number 0 or more

args.name: number2
args.about: another whole number 0 or more

about: Gives the bits that are on in both numbers.

example.why: 13 is 01101 and 25 is 11001; both have the 8 and 1 bits on, so 9.

name: BITLSHIFT

args.name: number
args.about: a whole number 0 or more

args.name: shift_amount
args.about: how many bits to move it by

about: Moves the bits of a number to the left, which doubles it once for each place.

example.why: 4 is 100 in binary; two places left is 10000, which is 16.

notes: A negative shift moves right, like BITRSHIFT.

name: BITOR

args.name: number1
args.about: a whole number 0 or more

args.name: number2
args.about: another whole number 0 or more

about: Gives the bits that are on in either number.

example.why: 5 is 101 and 3 is 011; either has each bit on, so 111 = 7.

name: BITRSHIFT

args.name: number
args.about: a whole number 0 or more

args.name: shift_amount
args.about: how many bits to move it by

about: Moves the bits of a number to the right, which halves it once for each place.

example.why: 13 is 1101 in binary; two places right is 11, which is 3.

notes: A negative shift moves left, like BITLSHIFT.

name: BITXOR

args.name: number1
args.about: a whole number 0 or more

args.name: number2
args.about: another whole number 0 or more

about: Gives the bits that are on in one number but not both.

example.why: 5 is 101 and 3 is 011; the bits that differ are 110 = 6.

name: COMPLEX

args.name: real_num
args.about: the real part

args.name: i_num
args.about: the imaginary part

args.name: suffix
args.about: "i" or "j" ("i" if left out)

about: Makes a complex number from its real and imaginary parts.

example.why: Real part 3 and imaginary part 4 make 3+4i.

name: IMABS

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the size (modulus) of a complex number.

name: IMAGINARY

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the imaginary part of a complex number.

example.why: The part with the i is 4.

name: IMARGUMENT

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the angle of a complex number, in radians.

example.why: 1+i points at 45°, which is π/4 radians.

name: IMCONJUGATE

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Flips the sign of the imaginary part of a complex number.

name: IMCOS

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the cosine of a complex number.

name: IMCOSH

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the hyperbolic cosine of a complex number.

name: IMCOT

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the cotangent of a complex number.

name: IMCSC

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the cosecant (1 over the sine) of a complex number.

name: IMCSCH

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the hyperbolic cosecant (1 over sinh) of a complex number.

name: IMDIV

args.name: inumber1
args.about: the complex number to divide

args.name: inumber2
args.about: the complex number to divide by

about: Divides one complex number by another.

name: IMEXP

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives e raised to a complex number.

name: IMLN

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the natural logarithm of a complex number.

example.why: ln|3+4i| = ln 5 = 1.609, and the angle is 0.927 radians.

name: IMLOG10

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the base-10 logarithm of a complex number.

example.why: log10 of 3+4i: log10 5 = 0.699, plus the angle over ln 10.

name: IMLOG2

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the base-2 logarithm of a complex number.

example.why: log2 of 3+4i: log2 5 = 2.322, plus the angle over ln 2.

name: IMPOWER

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

args.name: number
args.about: the power to raise it to

about: Raises a complex number to a power.

name: IMPRODUCT

args.name: inumber1
args.about: a complex number

args.name: inumber2
args.about: more complex numbers to multiply by

about: Multiplies complex numbers together.

name: IMREAL

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the real part of a complex number.

example.why: The part without the i is 6.

name: IMSEC

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the secant (1 over the cosine) of a complex number.

name: IMSECH

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the hyperbolic secant (1 over cosh) of a complex number.

name: IMSIN

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the sine of a complex number.

name: IMSINH

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the hyperbolic sine of a complex number.

name: IMSQRT

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the square root of a complex number.

name: IMSUB

args.name: inumber1
args.about: the complex number to take from

args.name: inumber2
args.about: the complex number to take away

about: Takes one complex number away from another.

name: IMSUM

args.name: inumber1
args.about: a complex number

args.name: inumber2
args.about: more complex numbers to add

about: Adds complex numbers together.

name: IMTAN

args.name: inumber
args.about: a complex number as text, like "3+4i"

about: Gives the tangent of a complex number.

name: CONVERT

args.name: number
args.about: the amount to convert

args.name: from_unit
args.about: its unit, like "mi", "kg" or "C"

args.name: to_unit
args.about: the unit to convert to

about: Converts an amount from one unit to another, like miles to kilometres.

example.why: A mile is 1.609344 km, so 26.2 miles is 42.16 km.

notes: Both units must measure the same thing (length, weight, temperature…), or it gives #N/A.

name: DELTA

args.name: number1
args.about: a number

args.name: number2
args.about: the number to compare with (0 if left out)

about: Gives 1 when two numbers are equal and 0 when they aren't.

name: GESTEP

args.name: number
args.about: the number to test

args.name: step
args.about: the threshold (0 if left out)

about: Gives 1 when a number is at or above a threshold, otherwise 0.
